newsitem.title: CANADA: SLIGHT CHANCE OF FROST IN SOUTH ALBERTA SUNDAY - EC.
newsitem.headline: SLIGHT CHANCE OF FROST IN SOUTH ALBERTA SUNDAY - EC.

text.p: A slight chance of frost was forecast for southern Alberta's grainbelt Sunday morning, an Environment Canada meteorologist said on Wednesday.
"There may be a possibility of frost over southern Alberta when a ridge of high pressure settles over that region Sunday morning," meteorologist Mike Russo said.
Harvesting was general across southern Alberta this week. The arrid region, where many fields are irrigated, produces mainly cereal grains or is used as grazing land for cattle.
"It's a very slight chance, I don't think it'll happen," Russo added.
A high pressure system over southern Saskatchewan and Manitoba Wednesday morning lead to cool overnight temperatures.
Wasagaming, in western Manitoba's Riding Mountain National Park, reported 0 Celsius (32 F) for two hours and was the coldest spot on the Prairie grainbelt.
Southern Saskatchewan reported overnight lows between +3.0 to +7.0 Celsius, Russo said.
Alberta's overnight lows dropped to the low teens Celsius.
